tour.overview:
For two thousand years Karnak was the greatest religious centre in Egypt, the home of the god Amun-Ra, and every pharaoh who could afford it added a gate, a hall or an obelisk. The result is the largest temple complex ever built: a city of pylons, courts and sanctuaries covering more than 200 acres. Its heart, the Great Hypostyle Hall, holds 134 sandstone columns, the tallest about 21 metres high, still carved and painted with the deeds of Seti I and Ramesses II. Three kilometres to the south stands Luxor Temple, where the statue of Amun came each year in a river festival, linked to Karnak by an avenue lined with hundreds of sphinxes.

This private afternoon visits both with a licensed Egyptologist, in the best order and the best light. You explore Karnak as the heat eases, walk part of the restored Avenue of Sphinxes in the golden hour, and arrive at Luxor Temple as the sun sets and the floodlights turn its colonnades amber. It pairs perfectly with a West Bank morning.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 5 hours
• Start and end: your hotel or Nile cruise boat in Luxor
• Type: private tour with car, driver and licensed Egyptologist guide
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; flat walking on sand and stone paving

WHAT YOU SEE
• Karnak Temple: the ram-headed sphinxes, the Great Hypostyle Hall, the obelisks of Thutmose I and Hatshepsut, and the sacred lake.
• Part of the Avenue of Sphinxes.
• Luxor Temple at sunset and after dark.

WHY THIS WORKS
Karnak is at its best in the softer afternoon light, and Luxor Temple is at its most magical just after sunset. Timing the tour this way also keeps you out of the midday heat.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Luxor, Nile cruise passengers, couples, families and photographers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the royal tombs and Hatshepsut's temple, see our West Bank tour. For both banks in one long day, ask us to combine them.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Wear comfortable shoes and bring a hat for the first hour and a light layer for the evening in winter. Photography is allowed throughout. Karnak's evening sound and light show can be added on request.

days.name: Karnak, the Avenue of Sphinxes and Luxor Temple
days.description:
What to expect: a private afternoon and evening on the East Bank with an Egyptologist, tickets to Karnak and Luxor Temple, and the temples at sunset.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 14:30 from your hotel or cruise boat and drive along the Corniche to Karnak. You enter between two rows of ram-headed sphinxes, the ram being the sacred animal of Amun, and pass through the unfinished First Pylon into the great court. Then comes the moment Karnak is famous for: the Great Hypostyle Hall, a forest of 134 columns shaped like papyrus stems, the twelve central ones about 21 metres tall, with traces of their original colours still visible high above. Your guide explains how it was built under Seti I and Ramesses II and reads the battle scenes on the outer walls. Further in you see the obelisk of Thutmose I and the obelisk of Hatshepsut, at almost 30 metres one of the tallest still standing in Egypt, and finish at the sacred lake, where priests purified themselves, beside the giant granite scarab that visitors walk around for luck.

As the light turns golden, you drive south and walk part of the Avenue of Sphinxes, the processional road of nearly three kilometres that once linked Karnak and Luxor Temple and reopened in 2021 after decades of excavation. Every year, during the Opet festival, the statue of Amun was carried along it to visit his southern temple.

You reach Luxor Temple around sunset. Built mainly by Amenhotep III and Ramesses II, it is entered through a pylon guarded by seated colossi of Ramesses and a single obelisk; its twin has stood in the Place de la Concorde in Paris since 1836. Inside, the colonnade of Amenhotep III and the great court glow as the floodlights come on, and above it all the medieval mosque of Abu al-Haggag still sits on top of the ancient walls. You are back at your hotel or boat at about 19:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times, adjusted to sunset)
14:30 – Pick-up from your hotel or cruise boat.
15:00 – Karnak Temple: sphinxes, Great Hypostyle Hall, obelisks and sacred lake (about 2 hours 15 minutes).
17:15 – Avenue of Sphinxes in the golden hour.
17:45 – Luxor Temple at sunset and after dark (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
19:30 – Return to your hotel or boat.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Sunset is around 17:00 in winter and 19:00 in summer, so we adjust the start time to your date.
• The Karnak sound and light show can be added after the tour on request.
• Optional: the Luxor Museum or the Mummification Museum on the Corniche.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed Egyptologist guide, tickets to Karnak Temple and Luxor Temple, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: sound and light show, Luxor Museum, dinner, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Why visit in the afternoon?
faq.answer: The light is softer, the heat eases, and Luxor Temple is at its most beautiful at sunset and under floodlights. It also leaves your morning free for the West Bank.

faq.question: How big is Karnak?
faq.answer: Huge: the whole complex covers more than 200 acres. We focus on the main Precinct of Amun with its finest monuments, which takes about two hours.

faq.question: Can we do the tour in the morning instead?
faq.answer: Yes. Karnak opens early and a morning visit works well, especially in summer. Luxor Temple is then seen in daylight.

faq.question: Do we walk the whole Avenue of Sphinxes?
faq.answer: No, it is almost three kilometres long. We walk the most impressive section and drive the rest.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the giant columns, the sphinxes and the scarab. The walking is flat and easy.

faq.question: Is it accessible for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Mostly. Paths are flat, though some floors are uneven sand or stone. Tell us in advance and we will plan the route accordingly.

faq.question: Can you collect us from a Nile cruise boat?
faq.answer: Yes. We collect you from your boat in Luxor and bring you back in time for dinner on board.

faq.question: Can we add the sound and light show?
faq.answer: Yes. Karnak's sound and light show runs in the evening in several languages. Tell us and we will book it and adjust the timing.

faq.question: Can we combine it with the West Bank?
faq.answer: Yes. Many guests do the West Bank in the morning, rest at lunchtime and join this tour in the afternoon.

faq.question: Is photography allowed?
faq.answer: Yes, photography is allowed throughout both temples without extra fees for phones and cameras.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and light clothes, a hat for the first hour, and a light jacket for winter evenings.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
